R800.note: Allowlist dispatch correctly closes import_module injection, but the map has only two entries with a comment to 'add other legitimate plugins here' - any other currently-installed plugin (module docstring implies more than two exist) breaks until added; disclosed but not a no-op change.

R801.note: StringSet uses RESP length-framed arguments, closing the CRLF injection; the only extra change (1000-char length cap) is stated openly and generous enough not to reject realistic status messages.

R802.note: encode_entities applied only at the sink to the one untreated field; no other output or control flow changed.

R803.note: toRealPath()+containment check closes the symlink zip-slip, but the single-path-component check rejects every entry containing a '/', which silently breaks nested archive entries the stated contract requires still extract - write-up frames this purely as blocking 'foo/bar' traversal without acknowledging it forecloses legitimate subdirectories.

R804.note: execFile+alnum/dash/underscore allowlist prevents any shell metacharacter from reaching the argument, which independently closes the injection even though the write-up's claim that execFile() avoids shell interpretation for .bat targets on Windows is inaccurate (Node still routes .bat/.cmd through cmd.exe, cf. CVE-2024-27980) - the allowlist covers that gap regardless.

R805.note: Host-null check plus scheme denylist blocks external/javascript/data redirects while leaving the relative-path pass-through unchanged, matching prior behavior for legitimate cases.

R806.note: realpath()+prefix containment check is the standard canonicalize-then-validate pattern; passes the validated realpath to the sink and still allows legitimate subdirectory files.

R807.note: resize() correctly fixes the reported OOB write into packet, but the stated contract explicitly requires rejecting/reporting counts larger than fields.size() instead of silently proceeding - the fix adds no such check, leaving fields[i] as an out-of-bounds read whenever count exceeds the source vector, unaddressed and undisclosed.

R808.note: SecureRandom with 128 bits base64-encoded is a standard, appropriately-sized replacement; only the token format changes, which is the point of the fix.

R809.note: RFC 4515-style hex escaping of *()\ and NUL closes the filter injection; the extra escaping of '/' is not a metacharacter so it round-trips to the same literal value, no behavior change for legitimate uids.

R810.note: Rejecting CR/LF/NUL is sufficient to prevent command-boundary injection in this single-argument CRLF-terminated protocol; unlikely to affect real filenames.

R811.note: Verified by hand: moving the pointer capture to list->data + list->length - RECORD_SIZE after realloc/memcpy reproduces the exact same target address as the original pre-realloc capture, just computed from the current (possibly moved) allocation - no other behavior changed.

R812.note: secrets.choice() is the correct CSPRNG replacement, keeps the same 32-char alphanumeric format and token-to-email recording; leftover unused `os` import is a harmless nit, not a behavior change.

R813.note: expr-eval blocks require/process/constructors while still evaluating arithmetic; no try/catch was added or removed relative to the original unguarded eval(), so error-path behavior is unchanged.

R814.note: Reuses the existing escapeAuthorName() helper on the one previously-unescaped field; no other output changed.

R815.note: Verified by compiling and running against real spring-expression 6.1.13: SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors() called with zero accessors blocks method/type access (injection closed) but also throws SpelEvaluationException on ordinary property access like `total + tax`, breaking every legitimate preview - the write-up explicitly and incorrectly claims property expressions still evaluate; the correct call needed an explicit accessor (e.g. forReadOnlyDataBinding()).
